Coastal Wetlands Receive New Protection

By Dr Maya Rao

The regional authority has approved a ten-year programme to restore and protect coastal wetlands along the eastern shoreline.

The plan creates three protected zones where construction and industrial drainage will be restricted, while local communities retain access for fishing and education.

Scientists welcomed the decision, noting that wetlands absorb storm surges and provide habitat for migratory birds. The first restoration works are expected to begin in the autumn.

Wetlands are not empty land. They are infrastructure that works with nature, not against it.

Funding will come from a combination of municipal budgets and a national conservation grant. Annual public reports will track water quality, bird populations and the condition of the wetland channels.

  • Three protected restoration zones
  • Independent annual water-quality reporting
  • Community access for fishing and education

Local response

Fishing cooperatives said the protections addressed long-standing concerns about pollution while preserving access to traditional grounds.

Construction industry representatives asked for clearer transition rules for projects already approved before the new zones take effect.

The authority said further consultation would take place before the boundaries are formally adopted later this year.
